root_cause: The navigation controller incorrectly sets aria-activedescendant to the list item's data value (its label) instead of the element's ID, causing assistive technologies to announce the wrong active option during arrow key navigation.
repair_strategy: In src/controllers/navigationController.js, replace the use of list[currentFocus].dataset.value with list[currentFocus].id when assigning the aria-activedescendant attribute within the update function.
expected_accessibility_effect: Arrow key navigation will now correctly update the input's aria-activedescendant to reference the active listitem's ID, enabling screen readers to announce the highlighted option as expected.
functional_risks: Any custom code that erroneously relied on aria-activedescendant containing the item's label may need adjustment, but the attribute is spec‑defined to hold an ID reference, so risk is low.
verification_requirements: After typing 'ma' and pressing ArrowDown once, the input's aria-activedescendant must equal 'autoCompleteJS_result_0'.
After a second ArrowDown, it must equal 'autoCompleteJS_result_1'.
Pressing Enter must submit the form with store value ['Marina Park'].
